meta.title: MCP server — Evento
meta.description: Connect Evento to Claude Desktop, Cursor, OpenClaw, and other MCP clients. List a user’s events and fetch event details from your AI agent with the Evento public MCP server.

hero.title: Connect Evento to your favorite agent
hero.description: The Evento public MCP server lets Claude Desktop, Cursor, and other MCP clients list a user’s events and fetch full event details — through the authenticated Evento public API, using your own API key.

highlights.apiKey: Your API key on every request
highlights.anyClient: Works with any stdio MCP client

cta.title: Give your agent your events
cta.description: Grab an API key, build the server, and look up Evento events right from your agent.

flow.title: A thin bridge between your agent and Evento
flow.description: The server is an MCP adapter over stdio. It turns tool calls into authenticated public API requests — no hosted MCP layer in between.

client.title: Your agent
client.detail: Claude Desktop, Cursor, or any client that supports stdio servers.

server.title: Evento MCP server
server.detail: Validates tool arguments, injects your API key, retries and normalizes responses.

api.title: Evento public API
api.detail: Each tool maps to a /public/v1 route. No direct database access, nothing persisted.

steps.list: Your client calls tools/list and the server returns the Evento tools.
steps.call: Your client calls tools/call with a tool name and arguments.
steps.validate: The executor validates the arguments and fills in the route placeholders.
steps.request: It sends an authenticated API request with a timeout and retry policy.
steps.normalize: The success or error payload is normalized back into an MCP response.

setup.title: Up and running in two steps
setup.description: Build the server once, then point any stdio-capable MCP client at it.

requirements.stdioClient: Any MCP client that supports stdio

build.title: Build the server
build.description: Clone and build, then set PUBLIC_API_KEY in .env. Run npm start to launch it on its own.

connect.title: Connect your client
connect.description: MCP clients share the same server block; OpenClaw picks up the Evento skill instead.

bestPractices.absolutePath: Use an absolute path in args
bestPractices.localEnv: Keep PUBLIC_API_KEY in client-local env config
bestPractices.restart: Restart the client after config changes

steps.s1: Add the server block to claude_desktop_config.json.
steps.s2: Point args at the absolute path of dist/index.js and set PUBLIC_API_KEY.

steps.s1: Add the same server block in Cursor’s MCP settings.
steps.s2: Point args at the absolute path of dist/index.js and set PUBLIC_API_KEY.

steps.s1: Find where your client configures stdio MCP servers.
steps.s2: Use the same command, args, and env fields shown here.
steps.s3: Restart the client after config changes.

steps.s1: OpenClaw reuses the Evento SKILL.md from its skills workspace.
steps.s2: Create the skill folder and copy SKILL.md into it.
steps.s3: If OpenClaw is already running, restart your session or gateway to pick it up.

troubleshooting.title: If something’s off
troubleshooting.description: The common fixes, plus how the server behaves when requests fail.

missingKey.title: Missing API key
missingKey.fix: Set PUBLIC_API_KEY in the MCP client’s env block.

toolsHidden.title: Tools not visible
toolsHidden.fix: Run npm run build, confirm dist/index.js exists, use an absolute path in args, then restart the client.

apiErrors.title: API errors
apiErrors.fix: Check the key’s scope and EVENTO_API_BASE_URL, then run the smoke check with a known username.

items.networkRetries: Retries timeouts, DNS failures and connection resets
items.isError: Failed calls return isError: true with a structured payload
items.noPersistence: No database access and no persistence in the MCP layer

items.localEnv: Keep API keys in local env config, never in source control

meta.title: Evento API — Build on top of your events
meta.description: Fetch public events, organizer feeds, and RSVP guest lists with the Evento Public API, or embed events anywhere with the no-auth, CORS-enabled Embed API.

hero.title: Build on top of your events
hero.description: Pull public events, organizer feeds, and RSVP guest lists into your own product — or drop events straight into any website with no-auth, CORS-ready embed endpoints.
hero.developerMode: Turn on Developer Mode in Settings → Advanced to keep API keys one tap away.

surfaces.title: Pick the right API for the job
surfaces.description: Use the Public API from your backend for rich data, and the Embed API straight from the browser for widgets.

public.name: Public API
public.tagline: Read-only event and user data for third-party server integrations.

points.p1: Authenticated with Unkey API keys via x-evento-api-key or Authorization: Bearer
points.p2: Rich payloads with creator metadata, links, contributions, and pagination
points.p3: Event details, organizer event lists, and RSVP guest lists
points.p4: Keep keyed requests server-side — never ship a key in client-side JavaScript

embed.name: Embed API
embed.tagline: No-auth, CORS-friendly responses for widgets and client-side embeds.

points.p1: No API key required — safe for client-side rendering
points.p3: Lean payloads with a computed status: upcoming, ongoing, or past
points.p4: Pairs with the evento-embed-react event card, list, and calendar components

explorer.title: Five GET endpoints, one consistent envelope
explorer.description: Explore each endpoint with real requests and response excerpts from the reference docs.

publicEvent.title: Fetch event
publicEvent.description: Retrieve detailed information for a published public event, including creator, links, and contribution metadata.

publicEventGuests.title: Fetch event guests
publicEventGuests.description: Retrieve RSVP guests for a published public event, filtered by RSVP status.

publicUserEvents.title: Fetch user events
publicUserEvents.description: List public events by username, with upcoming, past, or profile filters and pagination.

embedEvent.title: Fetch embed event
embedEvent.description: Retrieve a compact, embed-optimized event payload by ID — ready for event cards and detail embeds.

embedUserEvents.title: Fetch embed user events
embedUserEvents.description: Retrieve an embed-optimized event feed for a creator, with optional inclusive date bounds.

params.rsvpStatus: RSVP filter: yes, maybe, no, or all. Defaults to yes.
params.eventsType: Optional filter: upcoming, past, or profile.
params.eventsLimit: Results per page, max 100. Defaults to 20.
params.embedLimit: Number of events to return, max 100. Defaults to 50.

notes.publicEventGuests: Emails, phone numbers, and private contact details are never returned. Only guests linked to user profiles are included.
notes.embedUserEvents: Each event’s status is computed from its start and end timestamps: upcoming, ongoing, or past.

codePanel.copyFailedDescription: Copy it manually from the code block.

useCases.title: From widgets to community insights
useCases.description: Integration patterns straight from the Evento guides.

discovery.title: Event discovery platform
discovery.description: Aggregate events from creator accounts and public event IDs, then cache responses to keep pages fast.

widgets.title: Calendars & widgets
widgets.description: Render browser-safe calendars and event cards with the Embed API — no API key needed.

detailViews.title: Event detail views
detailViews.description: Build detail pages with creator metadata, Spotify and Wavlake links, and contribution handles.

community.title: Community intelligence
community.description: Measure RSVP conversion by status, verification mix, and repeat attendees across events.

profiles.title: Organizer profiles
profiles.description: Show a creator’s upcoming and past events on profile pages with the type filter.

sync.title: Calendar exports & sync
sync.description: Transform public schedules into external calendars and feeds, and refresh local caches.

contracts.title: Predictable by design
contracts.description: Both surfaces share the same success and error envelope and status-code conventions. Public API keys report their quota in response headers.

rateLimits.title: Rate limits
rateLimits.description: Over the limit you get a 429 — retry with exponential backoff and queue requests as you approach the daily quota.

envelope.title: Response envelope
envelope.description: Check success, log the human-readable message, and read your payload from data. Lists add pagination.

statusCodes.title: Status codes
statusCodes.description: Standard HTTP semantics. Private or unpublished resources return 404, and a missing or revoked key returns 401.

getStarted.title: Your first request is three steps away

developerMode.title: Enable Developer Mode
developerMode.description: Switch it on under Settings → Advanced to surface API keys in your settings.

createKey.title: Create an API key
createKey.description: Name it, then copy it right away — keys are shown only once. Up to 10 active keys per account.

firstRequest.title: Make your first request
firstRequest.description: Send the key in the x-evento-api-key header from your server. Successful calls return success: true with your payload in data.

quickstart.title: Quickstart
quickstart.description: Create an API key and make your first public API request.

authentication.title: Authentication
authentication.description: Header formats, auth flows by surface, and security practices.

dataModels.title: Data models
dataModels.description: Canonical event, guest, and pagination object schemas.
